You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# QuickJS

QuickJS is a small and embeddable JavaScript engine. It supports the ES2023 specification including modules, asynchronous generators, proxies, and BigInt.

## Features

- Small and easily embeddable: a few C files, no external dependency
- Fast interpreter with very low startup time
- Almost complete ES2023 support (including modules, async generators, proxies, BigInt)
- Passes nearly 100% of the ECMAScript Test Suite (test262)
- Can compile JavaScript to executables with no external dependency
- Garbage collection using reference counting with cycle removal
- Mathematical extensions: BigDecimal, BigFloat, operator overloading
- Built-in `std` and `os` modules for system interaction

## Usage

### Run a JavaScript file
```
qjs [options] file.js [args...]
```

### Evaluate an expression
```
qjs -e "console.log('hello')"
```

### Interactive REPL
```
qjs -i
```

### Options
```
-h  --help              list options
-e  --eval EXPR         evaluate EXPR
-i  --interactive       go to interactive mode
-m  --module            load as ES6 module (default=autodetect)
    --script            load as ES6 script (default=autodetect)
    --strict            force strict mode
-I  --include file      include an additional file
    --std               make 'std' and 'os' available to the loaded script
-T  --trace             trace memory allocation
-d  --dump              dump memory usage stats
    --memory-limit n    limit memory usage to n bytes
    --stack-size n      limit stack size to n bytes
-s                      strip all debug info
    --strip-source      strip the source code
-q  --quit              just instantiate the interpreter and quit
```

### std module
Provides: `printf`, `sprintf`, `open`, `popen`, `tmpfile`, `puts`, `getline`,
`readFile`, `loadFile`, `strerror`, `exit`, `gc`, `getenv`, `setenv`,
`unsetenv`, `getenviron`, `urlGet`, `parseExtJSON`, `SEEK_SET`, `SEEK_CUR`,
`SEEK_END`, `Error`.

### os module
Provides: `open`, `close`, `seek`, `read`, `write`, `isatty`, `ttyGetWinSize`,
`ttySetRaw`, `remove`, `rename`, `realpath`, `getcwd`, `chdir`, `mkdir`,
`stat`, `lstat`, `utimes`, `symlink`, `readlink`, `readdir`, `setReadHandler`,
`setWriteHandler`, `signal`, `exec`, `waitpid`, `pipe`, `kill`, `sleep`,
`setTimeout`, `clearTimeout`, `platform`, `Worker`.

## License

MIT License. Copyright (c) 2017-2025 Fabrice Bellard, Charlie Gordon.
2025-09-13
</output>

# Now let's be more systematic. Write a test suite.
cat > /tmp/run_tests.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
PASS=0
FAIL=0
run_both() {
    local expr="$1"
    local o=$(/tmp/qjs_orig -e "$expr" 2>&1)
    local m=$(./executable -e "$expr" 2>&1)
    if [ "$o" = "$m" ]; then
        PASS=$((PASS+1))
    else
        FAIL=$((FAIL+1))
        echo "DIFF: $expr"
        diff <(echo "$o") <(echo "$m") | head -4
    fi
}

# Basic arithmetic
run_both "console.log(1+2)"
run_both "console.log(10/3)"
run_both "console.log(Math.floor(-1.5))"
run_both "console.log(-Math.sign(-5))"

# Strings
run_both "console.log('a'+'b'+'c')"
run_both "console.log('abc'.length)"
run_both "console.log('abc'.split('').reverse().join(''))"

# Closures and scope
run_both "let x=10; function f() { return x; } console.log(f())"
run_both "let cnt = (function(){let c=0; return ()=>++c})(); console.log(cnt(), cnt(), cnt())"

# Prototypes
run_both "function Dog(n){this.n=n} Dog.prototype.bark=function(){return this.n+'!'}; let d=new Dog('Rex'); console.log(d.bark())"

# ES6 features
run_both "const [a,b,c]=[1,2,3]; console.log(a,b,c)"
run_both "const {x,y}={x:1,y:2}; console.log(x,y)"
run_both "console.log([...new Set([1,2,2,3,3,3])])"
run_both "let fn=(a,b=10)=>a+b; console.log(fn(5), fn(5,20))"

# Error types
run_both "try { null.x } catch(e) { console.log(e.name) }"
run_both "try { undefined() } catch(e) { console.log(e.name) }"
run_both "try { let a; a.b = 1 } catch(e) { console.log(e.name) }"

# Number formatting
run_both "console.log(1.0, 1.5, 0.1+0.2, 1/3)"
run_both "console.log(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, Number.MIN_VALUE, Number.EPSILON)"

# JSON

run_both "console.log(JSON.stringify({a:1,b:[2,3]}))"
run_both "console.log(JSON.stringify({a:1}, null, 2))"
run_both "console.log(JSON.parse('[1,2,3]'))"

# Async
run_both "(async () => { let x = await 42; console.log(x); })()"
run_both "Promise.resolve(1).then(v => console.log(v))"
run_both "Promise.all([1,2,3]).then(v => console.log(v))"

# Object
run_both "let obj = {a:1,b:2}; let c = Object.assign({}, obj, {c:3}); console.log(c)"
run_both "for (const [k,v] of Object.entries({a:1,b:2})) console.log(k, v)"

run_both "console.log([1,2,3].findIndex(x => x > 1))"
run_both "console.log([1,2,3].every(x => x > 0), [1,2,3].some(x => x > 2))"
run_both "console.log([1,2,3,4,5].slice(1,3))"

echo "Passed: $PASS, Failed: $FAIL"
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/run_tests.sh
bash /tmp/run_tests.sh

# More tests
run_both() {
    expr="$1"
    o=$(/tmp/qjs_orig -e "$expr" 2>&1)
    m=$(./executable -e "$expr" 2>&1)
    if [ "$o" = "$m" ]; then echo "OK"
    else
        echo "DIFF: $expr"
        diff <(echo "$o") <(echo "$m") | head -5
    fi
}

# Classes with inheritance
run_both "class A {} class B extends A {} let b = new B(); console.log(b instanceof A, b instanceof B)"
run_both "class P { constructor(x) { this.x = x; } } class C extends P { constructor(x, y) { super(x); this.y = y; } } let c = new C(1, 2); console.log(c.x, c.y)"

# Static methods
run_both "class A { static greet() { return 'hi' } } console.log(A.greet())"

# Class fields
run_both "class A { x = 10; constructor() { this.y = 20; } } let a = new A(); console.log(a.x, a.y)"

# getters/setters
run_both "class A { get x() { return 42 } set x(v) { this._v = v } } let a = new A(); console.log(a.x); a.x = 99; console.log(a._v)"

# For-of with entries
run_both "let a = ['x','y','z']; for (const [i, v] of a.entries()) console.log(i, v)"

# Complex destructuring
run_both "const {a: {b, c}} = {a: {b: 1, c: 2}}; console.log(b, c)"
run_both "const [[a], [b]] = [[1],[2]]; console.log(a, b)"

# Spread objects
run_both "let a = {x:1, y:2}; let b = {...a, z:3}; console.log(b)"

# Conditional
run_both "let x = 5; console.log(x > 0 ? 'pos' : x < 0 ? 'neg' : 'zero')"

# typeof undefined var
run_both "console.log(typeof undeclaredVar)"

# Array destructure with defaults
run_both "const [a=1, b=2] = [5]; console.log(a, b)"

# Error instance
run_both "let e = new Error('x'); console.log(e instanceof Error)"
run_both "let e = new TypeError('bad'); console.log(e instanceof TypeError, e instanceof Error)"

# Static methods
run_both "class A { static greet() { return 'hi' } } console.log(A.greet())"

# For-of with entries

# Complex destructuring

run_both "const [[a], [b]] = [[1],[2]]; console.log(a, b)"

# typeof undefined var

# Need to handle ArrayLit/ObjectLit as destructuring patterns in assignment
python3 << 'EOF'
with open('src/qjs.py') as f:
    src = f.read()

# Convert ArrayLit to ArrayPattern when used as assignment target
# Add conversion at eval_assign
old = '''    def eval_assign(self, node, env):
        op = node.op
        if op == '=' and node.left.type in ('ArrayPattern', 'ObjectPattern'):
            v = self.eval_expr(node.right, env)
            self.assign_pattern(node.left, v, env)
            return v'''
new = '''    def eval_assign(self, node, env):
        op = node.op
        left = node.left
        # Convert ArrayLit/ObjectLit to patterns
        if op == '=' and left.type in ('ArrayLit', 'ObjectLit'):
            left = self._expr_to_pattern(left)
        if op == '=' and left.type in ('ArrayPattern', 'ObjectPattern'):
            v = self.eval_expr(node.right, env)
            self.assign_pattern(left, v, env)
            return v'''
src = src.replace(old, new)

# Add _expr_to_pattern helper to convert expressions to patterns for assignment
helper = '''    def _expr_to_pattern(self, expr):
        if expr.type == 'Identifier':
            return Node('Ident', name=expr.name)
        if expr.type == 'ArrayLit':
            elems = []
            for el in expr.elements:
                if el is None:
                    elems.append(None); continue
                if el.type == 'Spread':
                    elems.append(Node('RestElement', arg=self._expr_to_pattern(el.arg)))
                    break
                if el.type == 'Assign' and el.op == '=':
                    elems.append(Node('BindingElement', target=self._expr_to_pattern(el.left), default=el.right))
                else:
                    elems.append(Node('BindingElement', target=self._expr_to_pattern(el), default=None))
            return Node('ArrayPattern', elements=elems)
        if expr.type == 'ObjectLit':
            props = []
            for p in expr.properties:
                if p.type == 'SpreadProp':
                    props.append(Node('RestElement', arg=self._expr_to_pattern(p.arg)))
                else:
                    key = p.key
                    val = p.value
                    default = None
                    if val.type == 'Assign' and val.op == '=':
                        default = val.right
                        val = val.left
                    props.append(Node('BindingProp', key=key, computed=p.computed, target=self._expr_to_pattern(val), default=default))
            return Node('ObjectPattern', properties=props)
        # Member expressions are used as assignment targets directly
        return expr

'''
src = src.replace('    def eval_lvalue(self, node, env):', helper + '    def eval_lvalue(self, node, env):')

# Also handle assign_target with patterns
src = src.replace(
    """    def assign_target(self, target, value, env):
        if target.type == 'Ident' or target.type == 'Identifier':
            env.set(target.name, value)
            return""",
    """    def assign_target(self, target, value, env):
        if target.type in ('ArrayLit', 'ObjectLit'):
            target = self._expr_to_pattern(target)
        if target.type == 'Ident' or target.type == 'Identifier':
            env.set(target.name, value)
            return"""
)

with open('src/qjs.py', 'w') as f:
    f.write(src)

# More diverse tests

# Conversion
run_both "console.log([1,2,3] + '')"

run_both "console.log((()=>42)())"

with open('src/qjs.py') as f:
    src = f.read()

# Add Object.is
src = src.replace(
    "    define_method(ctor, 'keys', keys, 1)",
    """    def object_is(this, args):
        a = args[0] if len(args) > 0 else UNDEFINED
        b = args[1] if len(args) > 1 else UNDEFINED
        if isinstance(a, (int, float)) and isinstance(b, (int, float)) and not isinstance(a, bool) and not isinstance(b, bool):
            import struct
            if a != a and b != b: return True
            if a == 0 and b == 0:
                # check sign
                return (struct.pack('>d', float(a))[0] & 0x80) == (struct.pack('>d', float(b))[0] & 0x80)
        return js_strict_eq(a, b)
    define_method(ctor, 'is', object_is, 2)
    define_method(ctor, 'keys', keys, 1)"""
)

with open('src/qjs.py', 'w') as f:
    f.write(src)
EOF
rm -f executable && ./compile.sh
./executable -e "console.log(Object.is(NaN, NaN), Object.is(0, -0))"

    o=$(/tmp/qjs_orig -e "$expr" 2>&1)

    if [ "$o" = "$m" ]; then echo "OK"

    fi
}

# Check some specific edge cases
run_both "console.log(1/0, -1/0, 0/0, 1/-0)"
run_both "console.log(typeof 1n)"
run_both "console.log(5n < 10n, 5n == 5, 5n === 5)"
run_both "console.log([1n,2n].map(x => x*2n))"

# Object getOwnPropertyNames
run_both "console.log(Object.getOwnPropertyNames({a:1, b:2}))"
run_both "console.log(Object.getOwnPropertyNames([1,2,3]))"  # includes 'length'

# Error stack properties
run_both "let e = new Error('hi'); console.log(e.message, e.name)"

# Chained calls
run_both "console.log([1,2,3].map(x=>x+1).filter(x=>x>2).map(x=>x*10))"
run_both "console.log(Object.keys({a:1,b:2}).reduce((o,k)=>(o[k+'x']=k, o), {}))"

# Regex replacement
run_both "console.log('hello world'.replace(/o/g, '0'))"
run_both "console.log('abc123def456'.replace(/(\\d+)/g, '[\$1]'))"
# Note: actual behavior for \$1 capturing group is tricky - skip

# Complex patterns
run_both "console.log(/abc/.test('xabc'))"
run_both "console.log('hello'.match(/l/g))"

# Array sort stability
run_both "console.log([{a:1,b:2},{a:1,b:1},{a:2,b:0}].sort((a,b)=>a.a-b.a).map(o=>o.b))"

# Short-circuit
run_both "let x = null; console.log(x && x.a)"
run_both "console.log(false || 'default')"
run_both "console.log(true && 'yes')"

# Math.round(-0.5) should be -0 (since -0.5+0.5=0, but sign preserved via special handling)
# In JS Math.round(-0.5) = -0, in my code I get 0
# The spec says Math.round rounds half towards +Infinity. For -0.5, result is 0. But the sign?
# Actually Math.round(-0.5) === -0 in JS. But -0 prints as -0 in my code.
# The issue: math.floor(-0.5 + 0.5) = math.floor(0) = 0. But should be -0.
# Fix: if x is in (-0.5, 0), result is -0
python3 << 'EOF'
with open('src/qjs.py') as f:
    src = f.read()

old = '''    def js_round(this, args):
        x = js_tonumber(args[0]) if args else float('nan')
        if x != x: return float('nan')
        if x in (float('inf'), float('-inf')): return x
        # JS round: round half to positive infinity
        return float(math.floor(x + 0.5))'''
new = '''    def js_round(this, args):
        x = js_tonumber(args[0]) if args else float('nan')
        if x != x: return float('nan')
        if x in (float('inf'), float('-inf')): return x
        # JS round: round half to positive infinity
        r = math.floor(x + 0.5)
        # Preserve -0 for values in (-0.5, 0]
        if r == 0 and x < 0:
            return -0.0
        return float(r)'''
src = src.replace(old, new)
with open('src/qjs.py', 'w') as f:
    f.write(src)
EOF
rm -f executable && ./compile.sh
./executable -e "console.log(Math.round(-0.5), Math.round(0.5))"

# Actually Math.round(-0.5) === -0 in JS. But -0 prints as -0 in my code.
# The issue: math.floor(-0.5 + 0.5) = math.floor(0) = 0. But should be -0.
# Fix: if x is in (-0.5, 0), result is -0
python3 << 'EOF'
with open('src/qjs.py') as f:
    src = f.read()

old = '''    def js_round(this, args):
        x = js_tonumber(args[0]) if args else float('nan')
        if x != x: return float('nan')
        if x in (float('inf'), float('-inf')): return x
        # JS round: round half to positive infinity
        return float(math.floor(x + 0.5))'''
new = '''    def js_round(this, args):
        x = js_tonumber(args[0]) if args else float('nan')
        if x != x: return float('nan')
        if x in (float('inf'), float('-inf')): return x
        # JS round: round half to positive infinity
        r = math.floor(x + 0.5)
        # Preserve -0 for values in (-0.5, 0]
        if r == 0 and x < 0:
            return -0.0
        return float(r)'''
src = src.replace(old, new)
with open('src/qjs.py', 'w') as f:
    f.write(src)
EOF

                elems.append(None)

run_both() {

        diff <(echo "$o") <(echo "$m") | head -5
    fi
}

# Object property enumeration order

# apply with arguments
run_both "function f() { return arguments.length } function g() { return f.apply(null, arguments) } console.log(g(1,2,3))"

# Exception message
run_both "try { JSON.parse('{') } catch(e) { console.log(e instanceof SyntaxError) }"

# Regex
run_both "let pat = /foo/g; let s = 'foo foo'; let m; while ((m = pat.exec(s)) !== null) { console.log(m[0], m.index) }"

# Arrow function with block
run_both "let f = (x) => { return x + 1 }; console.log(f(5))"

# IIFE
run_both "(function() { console.log('iife1') })(); (() => console.log('iife2'))()"

# Optional chaining with method call
run_both "let o = { a: { b: () => 42 } }; console.log(o?.a?.b?.())"

run_both "let o = { a: 0 }; console.log(o.a ?? 'default', o.b ?? 'default')"

# Rewrite make_ctor for errors to handle "this"
old = '''    def make_ctor(name, proto):
        def fn(t, a):
            err = JSObject(proto=proto, cls_name='Error')
            msg = a[0] if a and a[0] is not UNDEFINED else UNDEFINED
            if msg is not UNDEFINED:
                err.define_property('message', js_tostring(msg), True, False, True)
            err.define_property('name', name, True, False, True)
            err.define_property('stack', '', True, False, True)
            return err
        c = JSNativeFunction(name, fn, 1, proto=FUNCTION_PROTO, construct=True)
        c.define_property('prototype', proto, writable=False, enumerable=False, configurable=False)

# QuickJS

QuickJS is a small and embeddable JavaScript engine. It supports the ES2023 specification including modules, asynchronous generators, proxies, and BigInt.

## Features

- Small and easily embeddable: a few C files, no external dependency
- Fast interpreter with very low startup time
- Almost complete ES2023 support (including modules, async generators, proxies, BigInt)
- Passes nearly 100% of the ECMAScript Test Suite (test262)
- Can compile JavaScript to executables with no external dependency
- Garbage collection using reference counting with cycle removal
- Mathematical extensions: BigDecimal, BigFloat, operator overloading
- Built-in `std` and `os` modules for system interaction

## Usage

### Run a JavaScript file
```
qjs [options] file.js [args...]
```

### Evaluate an expression
```
qjs -e "console.log('hello')"
```

### Interactive REPL
```
qjs -i
```

### Options
```
-h  --help              list options
-e  --eval EXPR         evaluate EXPR
-i  --interactive       go to interactive mode
-m  --module            load as ES6 module (default=autodetect)
    --script            load as ES6 script (default=autodetect)
    --strict            force strict mode
-I  --include file      include an additional file
    --std               make 'std' and 'os' available to the loaded script
-T  --trace             trace memory allocation
-d  --dump              dump memory usage stats
    --memory-limit n    limit memory usage to n bytes
    --stack-size n      limit stack size to n bytes
-s                      strip all debug info
    --strip-source      strip the source code
-q  --quit              just instantiate the interpreter and quit
```

### std module
Provides: `printf`, `sprintf`, `open`, `popen`, `tmpfile`, `puts`, `getline`,
`readFile`, `loadFile`, `strerror`, `exit`, `gc`, `getenv`, `setenv`,
`unsetenv`, `getenviron`, `urlGet`, `parseExtJSON`, `SEEK_SET`, `SEEK_CUR`,
`SEEK_END`, `Error`.

### os module
Provides: `open`, `close`, `seek`, `read`, `write`, `isatty`, `ttyGetWinSize`,
`ttySetRaw`, `remove`, `rename`, `realpath`, `getcwd`, `chdir`, `mkdir`,
`stat`, `lstat`, `utimes`, `symlink`, `readlink`, `readdir`, `setReadHandler`,
`setWriteHandler`, `signal`, `exec`, `waitpid`, `pipe`, `kill`, `sleep`,
`setTimeout`, `clearTimeout`, `platform`, `Worker`.
